title: Aspecta / Service overview
description: SLO, RED signals, saturation, edge and TLS for the Aspecta service. Delivered as code from charts/aspecta/dashboards/ and imported by the Grafana sidecar - editing it in place is pointless, the next sync overwrites it.

links.title: Runbook
links.tooltip: What to do about each alert

panels.title: Error budget remaining
panels.description: Share of the error budget still unspent over the objective's window. The target, the budget and this figure all come from the aspecta:slo_* recording rules, so this panel and the burn-rate alerts cannot disagree.

panels.title: Availability (3d)
panels.description: The indicator itself: the share of requests not answered with a 5xx over the budget window. Green once it is at or above the objective.

panels.title: Objective
panels.description: The target the two panels to the left are measured against, read from the aspecta:slo_availability_target recording rule rather than typed in here.

panels.title: Burn rate (1h)
panels.description: How many times faster than sustainable the budget is being spent. 1x lasts exactly to the end of the window; 14.4x exhausts it in about two days, which is what AspectaErrorBudgetBurningFast pages on.

panels.title: Error budget burn rate
panels.description: Three windows of one measurement. The long window establishes that the budget is genuinely being consumed, the short one that it is still happening now - the alerts require both to agree, which is why all three are on the chart. The lines mark 1x and 14.4x.

panels.title: Requests
panels.description: Requests per second reaching the backend, all routes.

panels.title: Errors
panels.description: Requests per second answered with a 5xx.

panels.title: Error ratio (5m)
panels.description: Share of requests answered with a 5xx.

panels.title: p99 latency
panels.description: The catalogue is served from memory, so a sustained rise here points at CPU starvation or a saturated node rather than at the application.

panels.title: In flight
panels.description: Requests being served right now, summed over replicas. Latency rising while this stays flat is a slower backend; the two rising together is a queue forming.

panels.title: Response egress
panels.description: Response body bytes per second.

panels.title: Request rate by route
panels.description: Route is the registered pattern, never the raw path, so an object id cannot create a new series. Colours are pinned per route: a route that goes quiet must not repaint the others.

panels.title: Requests by status class
panels.description: Stacked, because the question here is how the total divides. Colours are the reserved status palette; 3xx keeps the categorical blue because a redirect is information rather than a fault.

panels.title: Latency quantiles
panels.description: One hue, light to dark. p50, p95 and p99 are an ordered family of the same measurement rather than three separate things, and a sequential ramp says so at a glance.

panels.title: p95 latency by route
panels.description: Which route is responsible when the aggregate p95 moves.

panels.title: CPU used against its request
panels.description: As a fraction of the container's CPU request, because that is the number the autoscaler acts on: the HPA targets 70% utilisation for the backend and 75% for the frontend, and utilisation in Kubernetes means percent of request. Deliberately not plotted against a limit - no CPU limit is set, so that ratio has no denominator and the panel showed nothing at all.

targets.expr: sum by (pod) (rate(container_cpu_usage_seconds_total{namespace="$namespace", container!=""}[5m])) / on (pod) group_left sum by (pod) (kube_pod_container_resource_requests{namespace="$namespace", resource="cpu"})

panels.title: Memory used against its limit
panels.description: Working set as a fraction of the limit. Reaching 1 is an OOM kill rather than a slowdown, which is why the line sits at 0.9.

targets.expr: sum by (pod) (container_memory_working_set_bytes{namespace="$namespace", container!=""}) / on (pod) group_left sum by (pod) (kube_pod_container_resource_limits{namespace="$namespace", resource="memory"})

panels.title: Replicas and the autoscaler
panels.description: Desired, available and the autoscaler's ceiling on one axis - they are the same unit, so they belong on the same chart. A gap between desired and available that does not close is a stuck rollout.

panels.title: Requests in flight per pod
panels.description: Per replica rather than summed: an even split means the Service is balancing, one pod carrying everything means it is not.

panels.title: Container restarts
panels.description: Restarts in the last hour per container. Flat at zero is the only good shape; a staircase is a crash loop.

panels.title: Requests at the edge, by host
panels.description: Measured at ingress-nginx rather than in the application, so it counts everything that reached the cluster - including the hosts the application knows nothing about.

panels.title: Plaintext requests redirected to HTTPS
panels.description: Every 308 the ingress issues is a client that arrived on port 80 and was sent to https. Non-zero is the redirect doing its job; a decline towards zero is HSTS taking over, because a browser that has seen the header stops trying plaintext on its own.

panels.title: TLS certificates
panels.description: Every certificate cert-manager manages, what signed it and how long it has left. Days left comes from the tls:certificate_expiry_days recording rule - the same figure the TLSCertificateExpiring alerts fire on.

panels.title: Time left on each certificate
panels.description: The same numbers as the table, shaped so the shortest bar is the one to look at. Leaf certificates renew at 30 days, so anything below that means renewal has not run.

panels.title: Catalogue objects
panels.description: Objects loaded from the embedded catalogue. Zero means a broken image reached production - the condition AspectaCatalogueEmpty fires on.

panels.title: Maintenance mode
panels.description: Set when a replica has been drained through the admin API. Left on, it silently removes capacity.

panels.title: Catalogue searches
panels.description: Split by whether the search returned anything. A rising share of empty results is a content problem, not an availability one.

panels.title: Alertmanager notifications received
panels.description: The application is its own alert receiver, so this is the last link of the chain: a rule fires, Alertmanager routes, the service acknowledges. Flat at zero while alerts are firing means the webhook or the NetworkPolicy between the namespaces is broken.

panels.title: Running versions
panels.description: One row per version in service. More than one row for longer than a rollout takes is a stuck deployment - what AspectaCatalogueRevisionMismatch alerts on.
